results.resolution: Keep the page as the climb of Mount Mathias from the Hoh River Trail (Glacier Meadows, Blue Glacier, Snow Dome, Glacier Pass, then the snow finger or the Mercury-Mathias col gullies and the Class 4 ridge); rename it West Face; carry out o03's text rewrite (re-checked against the live row; itinerary day 2 and the start time adjusted) plus the remaining traverse and 'upper Hoh Glacier' leftovers; null gain_ft, dist_km and the summit pin's distMi; remove the five traverse pins and the misplaced snow-finger hazard pin; add Glacier Meadows and Glacier Pass pins; clear the Sol Duc traverse line.
results.summary: Mathias is climbed from the Hoh River Trail and the Blue Glacier, so this page now describes that line throughout, with its own camp and pass pins, and drops the Sol Duc traverse figures, pins and drawn line.
results.evidence: LINE: The Mountaineers' Mathias & Mercury route (read through search extracts; the page 403s and is not archived) gives the two lines, the snow finger between Mathias and Glacier Pass or gullies to the Mercury-Mathias col, then Class 4 on the ridge, with Glacier Meadows as camp. Their 2020 Mathias/Mercury trip announcement (read in full from the Wayback copy) plans Day 1 Elk Lake, Day 3 'hike back to Blue Glacier, climb Mathias and Mercury, camp at Glacier Meadows', i.e. the Hoh River approach. Independently, the Olympic Mountain Rescue climbers' guide page for Mathias (read in full, Wayback 2023) lists Route 1 Grade II Class 4 via the West Face and Route 2 Grade II Class 4 via the Mercury-Mathias Col, glaciers Blue and Hoh, FA 1957 Eriksson/Hawkins; Wikipedia gives the easiest route as Class 4 via the West Face with the Blue Glacier below the west slope. The Blue Glacier is reached only from Glacier Meadows at the end of the Hoh River Trail. A full Bailey Range traverse report (climberkyle 2021) passes Blizzard Pass, Camp Pan and the Hoh Glacier below Glacier Pass but climbs no Mathias. Rule 2: the Hoh/Blue Glacier line is the documented one in current use; the traverse is kept only as a one-line mention in approach_variants[0].notes. APPROACH SIDE: Glacier Pass is the saddle between Mathias and the East Peak connecting the Blue Glacier (Glacier Meadows side) to the Hoh Glacier; so from Snow Dome the line goes up the upper Blue Glacier, not across the Hoh Glacier (that phrasing was the traverse's crossing from Camp Pan). Fixed in approach, pitch_detail[2], approach_variants[0].baseFinding, seasonal_hazards.crevasses and o03's itinerary day 2. PINS: Glacier Meadows camp — a GPS waypoint list from a 2021 Hoh/Olympus trip report gives 47.83251,-123.69143 (4,241 ft); OpenStreetMap's Glacier Meadows camp_site is 47.83235,-123.69144 — 18 m apart; USGS 3DEP ground 4,180 ft (used). Glacier Pass — USGS GNIS 47.79926,-123.68354; a 3DEP elevation grid I sampled puts the Mathias–East Peak saddle at ~47.799,-123.6825 (~6,130-6,180 ft), within ~80 m of GNIS; saddle height 6,140 ft (ListsOfJohn) and 6,102 ft key col 'Glacier Pass' (Peakbagger, lidar) — 6,140 used. Hoh trailhead pin (47.86028,-123.93472) is kept: OSM visitor center 47.86088,-123.93479 and the trip-report GPS 47.86047,-123.93429 agree. REMOVED: indexes 1-5 (High Divide, Eleven Bull Basin, Ferry Basin, Blizzard Pass, Camp Pan) are traverse points 2-12 km off the Hoh line; index 6 'Hoh Glacier / snow finger below Glacier Pass' sits at 47.8102,-123.6820 on ground of 5,420 ft (claims 6,500), 1.2 km NNE of Glacier Pass on the lower Blue Glacier icefall, ~730 m off the moraine-to-Snow-Dome-to-pass line — it is not where its name says and no source places a snow-finger point, so rule 1 removes it (the new Glacier Pass pin's note carries the snow finger). Summit pin kept; its distMi 28.5 (a traverse mileage) is set null. LINE DRAWN: gpx (363 points) starts and ends at 47.9548,-123.8349, the Sol Duc trailhead — the traverse; cleared. gain_ft 6,130 is below the Hoh line's own net rise (7,156 - 578 = 6,578 ft), so it cannot be this line's gain; dist_km 91.73 km (57 mi) is the traverse's ~55 mi total (row's own old itinerary totalNote). The only Hoh figures found (45 mi RT / 7,000 ft and 44 mi / 7,400 ft) both come from The Mountaineers — one source — so both columns are set null rather than to a figure. NAME: 'Bailey Range Scramble' named the traverse. 'West Face' is the Class 4 standard route in both the OMR guide (Route 1) and Wikipedia, matching the row's own face ('West Face') and fa ('(west face)'); it is the only route row on wa_mount_mathias. o03 ops re-checked against the live row: every expect equals and every find occurs once; the waypoints[6].note op was dropped (pin removed). Itinerary day 2 now says upper Blue Glacier; timing.recommendedStart is 'Before dawn from Glacier Meadows' instead of o03's '4:30 AM', which came from the traverse schedule. Also cleaned: overview ('Bailey Range' -> Mount Olympus massif; Peakbagger range: Olympus Group), beta, climate, comms, seasonal_hazards.weather, best_season (dropped an 'NPS gives' attribution), gear[7]. Left: bivy entries for Eleven Bull Basin/Ferry Basin/Camp Pan with role 'hidden' (they only suppress those camps), and 'traverse' used generically (e.g. glacier traverse).
sources: https://epqs.nationalmap.gov/v1/json (USGS 3DEP grid 47.796-47.804 N x 123.678-123.690 W: saddle at ~47.799,-123.6825, ~6,130-6,180 ft)

expect.cal: Requires an Olympic NP wilderness permit in the quota-controlled Sol Duc/Bailey Range corridor; the route is really only in condition July–September, and doing it while the Bailey Range snowfields and Mathias's snow finger still hold snow (rather than bare ice/scree) makes for much faster, safer travel.

days.note: Start at the Sol Duc trailhead, climb through Deer Lake to High Divide, then continue the ridgeline past Cat Basin to a high camp near Eleven Bull Basin. Packs are heaviest here — full glacier kit plus five days of food.
days.title: Sol Duc to High Divide / Eleven Bull Basin
days.objective: Reach a high camp beyond High Divide

days.note: Sidehill, mostly off-trail travel across the Baileys' famous narrow "catwalk" ridge sections below Mt Carrie and Stephen Peak, dropping into Ferry Basin to camp. Slow-going scree and heather traverses keep mileage low.
days.title: The Catwalks to Ferry Basin
days.objective: Cross the Baileys' exposed catwalks to Ferry Basin

days.note: Cross Bear Pass and Queets Basin, work around the Humes Glacier and Blizzard Pass, and drop to Camp Pan — the classic promontory camp used as the staging point for Mathias, Mercury, and Olympus.
days.title: Bear Pass to Camp Pan
days.objective: Reach Camp Pan overlooking the Hoh Glacier

days.note: Rope up and descend onto the Hoh Glacier, cross to Glacier Pass, stash packs, and climb the steep snow finger between Mathias and the pass to Class 4 rock on the summit ridge. Reverse the climb, re-rope for the Blue Glacier, and descend the moraine to camp at Glacier Meadows — the longest day of the trip.
days.title: Glacier Pass and the Mathias summit

expect.totalNote: A serious point-to-point traverse from Sol Duc to the Hoh, roughly 55 miles and ~11,000 ft of gain over 5 days, tagging Mathias's loose Class 4 summit near Glacier Pass along the way with a roped glacier crossing on summit day.

value.cal: Needs an Olympic National Park wilderness permit for the nights at Glacier Meadows. The route is in condition roughly July to September, and it goes faster and more safely while the snow finger still holds snow rather than bare ice or scree.

days.title: Hoh trailhead to Glacier Meadows
days.objective: Reach the Glacier Meadows base camp
days.note: The long, mostly gentle Hoh River Trail through the rainforest, climbing steadily only in the last few miles out of the valley. A washed-out section near the top is crossed on a fixed ladder. Packs carry full glacier kit.

days.title: Blue Glacier, Glacier Pass and the Mathias summit
days.objective: Climb Mount Mathias by the snow finger or the Mercury-Mathias col and return to camp
days.note: Take the way trail to the Blue Glacier moraine, rope up and cross the glacier to Snow Dome, then continue up the upper Blue Glacier to Glacier Pass, the saddle between Mathias and the East Peak of Mount Olympus. Climb the steep snow finger between Mathias and the pass, or the gullies to the Mercury-Mathias col, to Class 4 rock on the summit ridge. Reverse the climb and recross the glacier to Glacier Meadows. Mount Mercury is often added from the col.

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Walk back down the Hoh River Trail to the trailhead
days.note: A long, mostly downhill trail day back to the Hoh Rain Forest Visitor Center.

value.totalNote: An out-and-back from the Hoh: a long trail day in to Glacier Meadows, a roped glacier day to Glacier Pass and the summit ridge, and the walk out. Many parties add a spare day for weather or climb Mathias alongside Mount Olympus.
